entries.headline: Architecture: quote YAML-1.2 number-like strings in the collector's published architecture.yaml too?
body: The collector writes the merged dataset's YAML with plain yaml.safe_dump (tooling/collect.py:1163), the same YAML 1.1 dump this slice fixes in the two generators. Producer strings such as a firmware '9e10234' reach the merged dataset as strings and are written there plain. The dataset is published at https://architecture.webathome.org/data/v0.1/architecture.yaml, and the producer manual points producers at it. A YAML 1.2 reader such as js-yaml or yq v4 would read such a string as a number. architecture.json is unaffected. No known reader reads the YAML by 1.2 rules today: gen-architecture uses PyYAML and the viewer reads the JSON. Loading today's published YAML with js-yaml and comparing it against architecture.json found 0 mismatches. The plan scopes this writer out ('Any YAML writer other than the two generators R2's grounding names').
entries.consequence: none today; once live data puts a number-like string into the merged dataset, any YAML 1.2 reader of architecture.yaml reads it as a number while architecture.json stays right
entries.proposal: card — a cheap guard. The collector's published YAML should quote the same way the generators now do, but nothing misreads it today, so it does not belong in this slice.
entries.author: plan-reviewer, plan review r1: js-yaml load of the published architecture.yaml compared against architecture.json on 2026-10-03; tooling/collect.py:1163; plan_review_r1.md

entries.headline: Architecture service: a type error on an empty value prints an empty source scalar
body: For `a:` with no value where a string is expected, /api/validate now says `a:  (parsed as null) is not of expected type string` (double space, nothing quoted). For an empty sequence item the message starts with a space. Before P1 both read `value null is not of expected type string`. The locator returns source "" for an empty scalar (service/src/source-locate.ts), and the type translator only checks that the scalar exists (service/src/error-translate.ts:197-201). The line still points at the field.
entries.consequence: an author who leaves a required string blank gets a slightly garbled message; the line and 'parsed as null' still identify the problem
entries.author: code-reviewer, P1 r1, probe; phases/P1/code_review_r1.md F1

entries.headline: Architecture service: on a JSON body with duplicate keys, the error line and source scalar come from the wrong occurrence
body: JSON.parse keeps the last duplicate key; sourceLocator takes the first matching pair (service/src/source-locate.ts:36). For `{"a": 1, "a": "x"}` the locator returns line/source of `1` while the validated value is "x", so a type error would read `a: 1 (parsed as string 'x')`. YAML bodies are unaffected (js-yaml rejects duplicates with a 400). No estate generator emits duplicate JSON keys.
entries.consequence: on malformed hand-written JSON only, the error pairs the wrong source text with the parsed value and points at the earlier duplicate
entries.author: code-reviewer, P1 r1, probe; phases/P1/code_review_r1.md F2

entries.headline: ArgoCDTools aac-tools: no test pins that gen-architecture's written artifact goes through the quoting dumper
body: ArtifactQuotingTests (tests/test_gen_architecture.py) calls ga.dump_yaml directly. Reverting the write site at image/gen_architecture.py:1245 to plain yaml.safe_dump leaves the whole aac-tools suite green (100 tests OK, mutation run in review). The wiring is correct today; only the diff pins it.
entries.consequence: after a later edit of main()'s write block that drops the quoting, no test goes red, and number-like strings reach the validate service unquoted again, so it fails a repo's AaC Validate stage
entries.author: code-reviewer, P3, r1, phases/P3/code_review_r1.md F1

entries.headline: The driver left a scratch clone at /work/scratch/FieldnotesDeploy (`Target: github:pvginkel/FieldnotesDeploy`)
body: The driver cloned (or adopted) `/work/scratch/FieldnotesDeploy` for `Target: github:pvginkel/FieldnotesDeploy`; the slice's phases for that repo are branched, merged and pushed there.

Deleting it is safe once the slice's commits are on origin — the push check before the doc phase confirms that. The close-out session removes it then and says so under this entry; nothing is asked of the operator. A clone left in place is synced by every later preflight in this environment and adopted by the next `github:` target naming that repo.
entries.consequence: none — the clone is where the run works; left behind, it takes disk space and a sync in every later preflight, until the close-out session removes it.
